title: Anomalous Lattice Vibrations of Single- and Few-Layer MoS2
raman_evidence: Fig. 2b (PDF p.11, plot only, no table): E2g1 and A1g frequencies and their difference vs thickness for 1-6 layers and bulk; p.3 text: 1L E2g1 at ~384 cm-1 and the 1L frequency difference is ~3 cm-1 smaller than the 2L value; Fig. 2a spectra 1L-6L and bulk (360-430 cm-1); Fig. 3b (p.12) linewidths (p.5 text: E2g1 ~2.1 cm-1 independent of thickness, A1g 3 -> 6 cm-1 for 6L -> 2L); Fig. 4b (p.13) supported vs suspended 1L-4L; p.6 Methods: the Si Raman band at 520 cm-1 was used as internal frequency reference
sample_description: Mechanically exfoliated 1-6 layer and bulk 2H-MoS2 (natural molybdenite) on 285 nm SiO2/Si, layer number from contact-mode AFM; suspended 1L-4L over 1-1.5 um holes; ambient, backscattering
notes: paper.pdf is the arXiv v1 preprint (arXiv:1005.2509, 14 May 2010; 14 pages, same title without the hyphen), not the ACS version of record. The ACS article and its Supporting Information (freestanding vs supported linewidths) are behind the ACS paywall: needs_manual if the published version is required. title: Band Gap Engineering with Ultralarge Biaxial Strains in Suspended Monolayer MoS2
raman_evidence: SI Table S1 (PDF p.24): E2g1 / A1g Raman shift rates under biaxial strain in cm-1 per %: monolayer -5.2 / -1.7, bilayer -4.2 / -1.3, trilayer -3.0 / -0.7; main text (PDF p.8): unstrained E2g1 at 385 and A1g at 405 cm-1, shift rates -5.2 (E2g1) and -1.7 (A1g) cm-1/%, Grueneisen parameters 0.68 (E2g1) and 0.21 (A1g); SI p.23: mode separation ~19 cm-1 (1L), 21.7 (2L), 23.7 (3L); Fig. 2c strain dependence of both peaks; both modes soften
sample_description: CVD-grown (and exfoliated) monolayer, bilayer and trilayer MoS2 membranes suspended over 8 um holes in SiOx/Si, biaxial strain from a pressure difference across the membrane, 0 to 5.6 %
notes: paper.pdf is the Boston University OpenBU author copy (35 pages = 1 repository cover page + main text + SI; same text as arXiv:1608.04264). Strain is biaxial, so both peaks shift in the same direction (the readout case in ARCHITECTURE.md). The ACS Nano-Letters correction Nano Lett. 2019, 19, 7548 (doi 10.1021/acs.nanolett.9b03591) exists; its content could not be read (ACS blocked), so check whether it changes the strain scale before copying the slopes.
